examples.scenario: Self-intersecting parcel polygon is rasterized without validity check.
examples.reason: Invalid geometries can produce incorrect spatial-intersection results.

examples.scenario: A polygon passes IsValid but neighboring parcel edges overlap.
examples.reason: Individual validity does not detect inter-feature coverage defects.

examples.scenario: MakeValid is applied silently before rasterization.
examples.reason: Repair can alter geometry structure and must have before/after provenance.

examples.scenario: MakeValid linework and structure return different shapes.
examples.reason: Repair algorithm is part of reproducibility.

examples.scenario: Lower-dimensional fragments are dropped after repair without recording.
examples.reason: Repair output dimensionality can change.

examples.scenario: Coverage cleaning snaps a parcel edge and result becomes canonical.
examples.reason: Cleaning mutates the source boundary.

examples.scenario: Simplify-coverage preserves shared edges but moves parcel vertices.
examples.reason: Topological preservation does not mean coordinate identity.

examples.scenario: Clip geometry CRS is omitted and coordinates are interpreted in the input CRS.
examples.reason: Clip geometry CRS must be explicit.

examples.scenario: Vector clipping changes a GeometryCollection into polygon parts silently.
examples.reason: Clipping can alter output geometry typing.

examples.scenario: Raster clip expands bounds to whole pixels and edge pixels enter extrema.
examples.reason: Pixel-rounded clip bounds are not the parcel membership rule.

examples.scenario: Raster clip outside source is allowed and synthesized pixels enter the mask.
examples.reason: Out-of-source pixels must fail closed.

examples.scenario: Warp cutline output is sampled as though it were the native raster.
examples.reason: Cutline/warp output can resample or change pixel support.

examples.scenario: Default center-membership and ALL_TOUCHED masks disagree at the parcel boundary.
examples.reason: Boundary policy materially changes included pixels.

examples.scenario: ALL_TOUCHED is enabled without recording feature order.
examples.reason: Overlapping edge outcomes can depend on input feature order.

examples.scenario: Mask replay uses 8-connectivity while original polygonize used 4-connectivity.
examples.reason: Diagonal connectivity changes derived regions.

examples.scenario: Mask polygon round-trip has same area but different boundary cells.
examples.reason: Area equality alone does not prove identical membership.

examples.scenario: pixel-info and gdallocationinfo map the same coordinate to different cells.
examples.reason: Independent pixel addressing must agree before terminal sampling.

examples.scenario: pixel-info uses bilinear interpolation during membership audit.
examples.reason: Membership audit must identify native source cells.

examples.scenario: A boundary-near pixel is selected solely because its center is close to the polygon edge.
examples.reason: Proximity is QA evidence, not the membership definition.

examples.scenario: Vector pipeline validation and cleaning are combined into one opaque stage.
examples.reason: Validation and mutation must be separately auditable.

examples.scenario: GDAL version changes between primary and replay runs.
examples.reason: Geometry/raster behavior must be replayed with a frozen runtime.

examples.scenario: GEOS version changes between validity and replay runs.
examples.reason: Validity/repair behavior is GEOS-backed and version provenance matters.

examples.scenario: Two masks produce the same extrema but different included pixel sets.
examples.reason: Terminal acceptance requires membership lineage, not only matching extrema.

examples.scenario: Numeric height difference is published before canonical geometry and dual-mask execution exist.
examples.reason: Real numeric output remains fail-closed until canonical execution evidence exists.
